The four rules this change introduces that no tool can enforce are implemented as prose at the point of the rule and listed in docs/harness-enforcement.md as items 15-18: a RowHandler must be idempotent per row; a DocumentHandler must not call a partner inside the apply transaction; whether a declared commit-policy is right for the domain; whether a deployment's FileScanner actually scans.

ALL_OR_NOTHING reads the bound-row artifact inside its single transaction, so it holds a database connection for the whole traversal. Unavoidable given what the policy promises, documented at ApplyPass, and the reason a large file on that policy belongs on a DEFERRED action - but not mechanically prevented.

The annotated error report only annotates rows within the action's reject-sample bound (default 100). A submission with more rejects than that gets a partially annotated workbook. Recorded at RejectCollector; a submission in that state has almost certainly tripped its reject threshold and been refused whole anyway.

A reactive upload (FilePart, Flux<DataBuffer>) and an upload taken as a raw byte[] request body are both invisible to RuleGroup.UPLOADS. No module in this platform is reactive, and a rule flagging every InputStream parameter would be suppressed everywhere within a week. Both blind spots are named in the rule's javadoc.
